reason: The cited evidence (E3) supports the general benefit of HIP for fatigue performance in metallic parts, but it is specific to SLM additive manufacturing, not MnNiSi-based materials. E1 and E2 discuss magnetocaloric properties of different material systems and do not address mechanical properties, HIP effects, or the specific MnNiSi system. Thus, the key premises linking HIP to mechanical improvement in MnNiSi while preserving magnetocaloric effect lack direct, specific prior evidence.
premises: HIP post-treatment reduces porosity and microcracks, improving fatigue resistance and ductility in metallic materials
MnNiSi-based materials exhibit large magnetocaloric effect but suffer from mechanical brittleness and internal defects
HIP parameters can be controlled to avoid phase transformations that would degrade the magnetocaloric effect
Reducing internal defects does not significantly alter the bulk phase responsible for the magnetocaloric effect
Mechanical densification post-treatments are effective for fatigue performance improvement in additively manufactured parts
